habitat: Woodland, thornveld and riverine forest, often in large colonies. Nomadic when not breeding.
summary: A common resident. The breeding male has a spotted back, red eyes and a black bill. The northern race has an entirely black head. The southern race has a yellow crown, with black only on the face and throat. Newman does not say which race occurs in Kruger. The identification line says the female has red eyes and a pinkish bill. The description says the female has brown eyes, a yellow breast and white underparts, and that the non-breeding male is like the female but keeps the red eyes. The eye colour is left unset. The call is a husky swizzling. The Kemp paper name Spottedbacked Weaver and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Southern Masked Weaver has a plain back and a pointed black bib. Village Weaver has a spotted back.

head.pattern: Newman does not assign a race to Kruger. The northern race has an entirely black head. The southern race has a yellow crown, with black only on the face and throat.

upperparts.pattern: Spotted back. The identification line says the mantle is yellow-speckled and the wings are dark.

wings.pattern: Dark wings. Newman does not name the dark colour.

head.pattern: The identification line says the eyes are red and the bill is pinkish. The description says the eyes are brown. The iris is left unset.

underparts.pattern: Yellow throat and breast, whitish belly. No speckled mantle and no mask.

head.pattern: Non-breeding male resembles the female but retains the red eyes.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. It is nomadic when not breeding. The female eye colour conflicts: red on the identification line, brown in the description, so the iris is unset. Newman does not assign the northern or southern race to Kruger. A watermarked frame was not used. No female photograph and no flight photograph were found. Population figures and the Kemp name Spottedbacked Weaver were left unchanged.
